events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 841 PM MDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 17 miles south of Stratton to 11 miles south of
Ruleton to 6 miles north of Wallace, moving north at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Cheyenne Wells, Sharon Springs, Weskan, Wallace, and Arapahoe.

This includes Highway 385 between mile markers 147 and 183.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1042 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms produced heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain fell.
Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected. Flash flooding is possibly ongoing already.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Flemingsburg, Fairview, Pecks Ridge, Craintown, Tilton,
Elizaville, Sherburne, Nepton, Cowan, Pebble, Bethel, Poplar
Plains, Ewing and Flemingsburg Junction.

Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S affecting Clinton and Scott

Counties.

Iowa River at Marengo affecting Iowa and Benton Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S.

* WHEN...From Saturday morning to Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, water affects County Road E63 north of the
river near Toronto and affects the lowest roads in Buena Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 9.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage Saturday morning
to 11.2 feet Saturday afternoon. It will then fall below flood
stage early Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
